Under the standard node2vec formulation, there is no backdoor-adjustment equation because node2vec is a biased random-walk embedding method, not a structural causal model. If one were to impose a causal interpretation and treat the random-walk transition as an intervention on the next-node choice, a generic backdoor-adjustment form would be

P(Y \mid do(X=x)) = \sum_z P(Y \mid X=x, Z=z) P(Z=z),

or, in continuous form,

P(Y \mid do(X=x)) = \int P(Y \mid X=x, Z=z) \, p(z) \, dz,

where Z is a valid adjustment set that blocks all backdoor paths from X to Y. However, this is a hypothetical causal reformulation, not part of the original node2vec algorithm. In node2vec itself, the key mechanism is a biased random walk procedure that interpolates between breadth-first and depth-first exploration using parameters p and q, and the learned node embeddings are optimized from the resulting walk corpus with a skip-gram-style objective.

So the most accurate answer is: node2vec does not have an official backdoor-adjustment equation; the causal backdoor formula above is only a generic causal-inference template, not a node2vec-specific derivation.
